title: Entertainment Majors Back Stability AI’s $76M Round
summary: EA and three global music groups joined Stability AI’s Series B, tying its next phase more closely to licensed creative production.
body:
## Rights holders become shareholders

Stability AI has raised $76 million in a Series B whose new investors include Electronic Arts, Sony Music Group, Universal Music Group and Warner Music Group. AMD Ventures and Pacific Alliance Ventures also participated, alongside returning backers including Coatue, Greycroft, Kadmos Capital, Sean Parker and Eric Schmidt.

The company says it has now secured $232 million under chief executive Prem Akkaraju since he took over in June 2024. That total includes two equity rounds and convertible notes, rather than representing a single cash investment. Stability did not disclose its valuation, financial performance or the ownership acquired by the new investors.

The capital is earmarked for creative-production products, applied research and an expanded professional-services business. Stability now develops image, video, 3D and audio systems, including Stable Audio 3.0, an open-weight music-model family trained on licensed material. Coatue co-founder Thomas Laffont is also joining its board.

## A different compact for generative media

The investor roster is more important than the headline amount. EA, Universal and Warner already had strategic relationships with Stability, while Sony Music is joining as a new investor. Their equity participation gives Stability direct access to organizations controlling valuable games, recordings and production workflows, but may also pull its roadmap toward bespoke commercial tools and away from the broadly accessible image-model releases that built its reputation.

The financing marks a further turn in generative media's relationship with copyright owners. Rather than treating studios and labels only as licensors or legal adversaries, Stability is making several of them financial stakeholders in the tools that could reshape creative production. That alignment could improve access to licensed training data and accelerate adoption inside established media companies. It does not eliminate the harder questions: the company still must show sustainable revenue, explain how value reaches individual creators, and demonstrate that strategic investors will tolerate products that compete with existing production labor and licensing markets.
title_zh: 三大音乐集团与EA参投Stability AI新融资
summary_zh: Stability AI完成7600万美元B轮融资，EA及三大国际音乐集团入股，其发展路线进一步转向授权内容与专业制作。
body_zh:
## 内容权利方成为股东

Stability AI完成7600万美元B轮融资，新投资者包括Electronic Arts、索尼音乐集团、环球音乐集团和华纳音乐集团。AMD Ventures与Pacific Alliance Ventures亦有参与；Coatue、Greycroft、Kadmos Capital、肖恩·帕克和埃里克·施密特等现有投资者继续跟投。

公司称，自普雷姆·阿卡拉朱于2024年6月接任首席执行官以来，已累计获得2.32亿美元资金。该数字包含两轮股权融资和可转换票据，并非本轮全部为现金注资。Stability AI没有披露本轮估值、经营业绩或新投资者获得的股权比例。

新资金将用于发展创意制作产品、加强应用研究并扩充专业服务业务。Stability AI目前覆盖图像、视频、3D和音频生成，其中Stable Audio 3.0是一组使用完整授权数据训练的开放权重音乐模型。Coatue联合创始人托马斯·拉丰也将加入公司董事会。

## 生成式媒体形成新的利益组合

相较融资金额，投资者名单更值得关注。EA、环球音乐和华纳音乐此前已与Stability AI建立战略合作关系，索尼音乐则是新加入的投资者。这些公司控制着大量游戏、录音版权及成熟制作流程，入股能够让Stability AI更直接地接触优质授权数据和真实生产场景；与此同时，其产品路线也可能更偏向定制化商业工具，弱化当年帮助公司建立影响力的普惠型图像模型。

这轮融资说明，生成式媒体公司与版权方的关系正在改变：影视、游戏和唱片企业不再只是授权方或潜在诉讼对手，也开始分享工具商业化带来的收益。利益绑定有望加快授权训练数据的获取，并推动生成工具进入大型内容企业。但融资并未解决所有问题——Stability AI仍需证明收入模式可以持续，说明普通创作者如何分享新增价值，并面对这些工具可能冲击现有制作岗位及版权授权市场的矛盾。
